translationRepairs: In the eleventh year of Datong he was granted Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Great General Who Conquers the West, and Grand Mausoleum with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes.

In the eleventh year of Datong he was granted Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Great General Who Conquers the West, and the privilege of establishing a separate office with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Dukes.

s0065 ends with 開府儀同三司, the privilege of opening a headquarters with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes; "Grand Mausoleum" invents a mausoleum sense absent from the Chinese, and the proposed idiomatic rendering restores the honorific accurately.
In the eleventh year of Datong he was granted Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Great General Who Conquers the West, and Grand Mausoleum with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes.

In the eleventh year of Datong he was granted Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Great General Who Conquers the West, and [the right of] opening an office with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes.

The same s0065 phrase 開府儀同三司 means opening an office with ceremony equal to the Three Dukes, not a "Grand Mausoleum"; the bracketed literal clarifies the granted right without changing the other titles.
During the Taiping era, when Hou Jing rebelled, Ji did not come to the rescue.
During the Taiqing era, when Hou Jing rebelled, Ji did not come to the rescue.
s0067 has 及太清中; 太清 is the Liang era Taiqing, whereas Taiping would be 太平, so the proposed romanization corrects a real reign-name error.
During the Taiping era, when Hou Jing rebelled, Ji did not come to the rescue.
During the Taiqing era, when Hou Jing rebelled, Ji did not come to the rescue.
Literal field for s0067 likewise misreads 太清 as Taiping; Taiqing matches the Chinese era name and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
In the fourth month of summer in the fifth year of Taiping, Ji led his army east to Ba commandery, claiming to attack Hou Jing but intending to seize Jing and Shan.
In the fourth month of summer in the fifth year of Taiqing, Ji led his army east to Ba commandery, claiming to attack Hou Jing but intending to seize Jing and Shan.
s0076 opens 太清五年夏四月; again 太清 is Taiqing, not Taiping, and the rest of the proposed sentence matches the Chinese march narrative.
In the fourth month of summer in the fifth year of Taiping, Ji led his army east to Ba commandery, claiming to attack Hou Jing but intending to seize Jing and Shan.
In the fourth month of summer in the fifth year of Taiqing, Ji led his army east to Ba commandery, claiming to attack Hou Jing but intending to seize Jing and Shan.
The literal for s0076 repeats the same 太清五年 era error; Taiqing is the correct romanization and no other meaning is altered.
When the palace city fell, the Taqing era was restored and Zhengde was reduced to Grand Marshal.
When the palace city fell, the Taiqing era was restored and Zhengde was reduced to Grand Marshal.
s0149 has 復太清之號; Taqing drops the medial i of Taiqing and is not a valid reading of 太清, so the proposed fix is a necessary romanization correction.
When the capital fortress fell, the Taqing era name was restored and Zhengde was demoted to Grand Marshal.
When the capital fortress fell, the Taiqing era name was restored and Zhengde was demoted to Grand Marshal.
Literal s0149 likewise restores the era name from Taqing to Taiqing for 太清, matching the Chinese without other changes.
In the Taqing disaster Xiao Ji held the wealth of Yong and Shu yet never rushed to the throne's rescue or kept a son's or subject's duty;
In the Taiqing disaster Xiao Ji held the wealth of Yong and Shu yet never rushed to the throne's rescue or kept a son's or subject's duty;
s0185 begins 太清之寇; Taqing is a misspelling of Taiqing for 太清, and the proposed idiomatic line otherwise preserves the historian's judgment.
In the Taqing calamity, Xiao Ji held the resources of Yong and Shu, yet did not hasten to the king's aid in crisis or fulfill a subject's and son's duty;
In the Taiqing calamity, Xiao Ji held the resources of Yong and Shu, yet did not hasten to the king's aid in crisis or fulfill a subject's and son's duty;
The literal appraisal likewise requires Taiqing for 太清之寇; Taqing is unsupported, and the replacement is otherwise faithful.
